schema.title: Corpus ontology
schema.hint: An LLM will propose entity types and typed relations (with domain/range). You can edit, add or drop them. Skipping leaves extraction in open-vocab mode (PERSON/ORG/CONCEPT/MISC).
schema.skipHint: Optional step — extraction will run open-vocab
schema.errorNoCorpus: Corpus not set — go back to step 1
schema.softTitle: Soft mode: domain/range doesn't drop edges
schema.softBody: If an edge's predicate matches a schema relation but its endpoints don't satisfy the relation's domain/range, the edge is kept and tagged attributes.ill_typed=true. Open-vocab extraction often produces edges between type pairs that strict ontology rules reject (e.g. COMPONENT-«analyzes»-OFFER under ANALYZES: TEAM_MEMBER→METRIC). Strict mode (script flag) drops them, losing ~30% of typed edges. ill-typed edges are filterable in the graph view.

pipeline.title: Build pipeline
pipeline.hint: Pick a builder, a cleaner chain and a clusterer. Green-marked options are recommended by the EDA step.
pipeline.cleanerNote: Application order = click order. These cleaners run one after another, right after the builder and before the clusterer.
pipeline.clusterNoneHint: Don't run a clusterer on this build.
pipeline.projectorHint: After community detection, derives per-layer NPMI-weighted co-occurrence edges and keeps the 2n-5n most locally-significant ones via a disparity filter — kills the megahub and gives a readable graph per layer.
pipeline.projectorNoneHint: Skip backbone projection. The graph keeps only its original inter-layer and ENTITY_RELATION edges.
pipeline.projectorParamsHint: Projector parameters (e.g. the two-mode projection normalization).
pipeline.outputLanguageHint: Language used to normalise entity names and generate summaries.
pipeline.llmHint: Bring-your-own OpenAI-compatible server (OpenAI, Deepseek, OpenRouter, or local Ollama / llama.cpp / vLLM). Leave the fields empty to fall back to the server-default LLM.
pipeline.llmApiKeyHint: Local servers usually accept any value (or none). Never stored on the backend.

review.title: Confirm and run
review.hint: Check the parameters. If everything is correct, press "Run build" — the corpus and documents will be persisted, builder/cleaner/clusterer will run synchronously and you'll land on the new variant page.

ask.modeSingleDescription: Good for quick checks and regression tests: one reasoner, one variant, minimum LLM calls.

walkthrough.step1Body: Every graph is built from a corpus. This is the graph you picked — let's tour what you can do here.
walkthrough.step2Body: Chunks, entities, communities and topics are stacked layers. Use the toolbar (or keys 1–4 / Tab) to focus one layer at a time.
walkthrough.step3Body: The delta legend keeps one grammar for three sources: time diffs, query evidence, and edit cascades. Watch it light up as you explore.
walkthrough.step4Body: Click a node to open its drawer: summary, applicable tools, rename, and read-only bitemporal history.
walkthrough.step5Body: Open the suggestions sidebar to run agents and accept or reject curation proposals. Every accept ripples across the graph.
walkthrough.step6Body: Toggle the timeline to scrub instants or diff two moments, then ask the graphs a question from the wizard.

timeline.axisValidTip: Valid time — when the fact was true in the world (event_time).
timeline.axisTxTip: Transaction time — when we learned the fact (ingested_at). ADR-0002.
